Muscle biopsies taken 21 hours after the exercise bout showed a significantly greater disruption in fibers from the eccentrically trained arms than in the concentrically trained arms. These findings underscore the fact that the repeated bout effect only attenuates the magnitude of muscle damage on a general level as opposed to preventing its occurrence when a novel routine is employed and leaves open the possibility that EIMD may contribute to hypertrophy in well-trained lifters. It seems that the key to this response is to provide a novel stimulus by altering training variables in an unaccustomed fashion.
